# GitClient

> GitClient is a free, open-source (MIT) desktop Git GUI for Linux and Windows that reproduces the Git tooling of JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm) as a standalone app: a commit log with branch graph, a Branches panel, a Commit tool window with hunk staging, an interactive rebase dialog and a 3-way merge conflict editor. Built with Electron, React and TypeScript; it runs the user's installed git (2.30+) and shows every command it executes.

Key facts:

- Platforms: Linux x64 (.deb for Ubuntu/Debian, AppImage, .tar.gz) and Windows 10/11 x64 (per-user installer, no admin). No macOS package yet.
- Install on Linux: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phil288/git-client/main/install.sh | bash`
- Install on Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phil288/git-client/main/install.ps1 | iex`
- Open a repository from a terminal: `gitclient .`
- Free and open source, no account, no telemetry; the only own network call is an optional update check against GitHub releases.
- Works with any Git host (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted) through the user's existing remotes, SSH keys and credential helpers.
- Alternatives it is often compared to: GitKraken, Fork, Sourcetree, Tower, GitHub Desktop, Sublime Merge, SmartGit, GitAhead, gitg, git-cola, lazygit. Unlike most, it is free, open source and runs on Linux.
